title: Kernel-aware KV prefetching and allocator hinting for long-context variants
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We've observed elevated peak GPU working set and fragmentation for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants when continuous batching and KV-residency interact with kernel allocation patterns. Current memory planner treats KV slices and intermediate allocations independently of the kernel execution characteristics, causing suboptimal packing for kernels that prefer contiguous memory or have high allocation churn.

Goal: Implement a kernel-aware KV prefetch and allocator-hinting mechanism plus a small runtime IPC to expose per-model memory profile hints. The runtime will use these hints to: 1) prefetch hot KV slices earlier and pack them into contiguous slabs when beneficial, 2) bias the hybrid slab allocator to place ephemeral tensors away from long-lived KV pages, and 3) coordinate with continuous batching to maintain low p99 latency while reducing fragmentation and peak memory. Target models: Llama-v2 variants, Mistral-large variants, Qwen long-context variants across 2k/16k/32k context lengths.

Why unique: This ticket couples kernel characteristics (e.g., vectorizable kernels that suffer when allocations are scattered) with KV residency policies and batching heuristics — an angle not covered by prior per-model memory profiles. It aims at runtime-level hints and prefetch scheduling rather than purely allocator or KV eviction rules alone.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiments show >=10% average peak GPU memory reduction across target models at 16k context compared to baseline (same batch shapes and tokens/sec),
No more than 3% drop in sustained throughput (tokens/sec) for validated batch shapes and model variants
p99 generation latency regression <= 5ms for low-latency tiers and <= 10ms for best-effort tiers
Eviction and rehydration rate for KV cache does not increase by more than 10% relative to baseline
Feature accessible via runtime config flag 'kernel_prefetch_v1' and can be toggled without restart for private/dedicated deployments
experiments: Baseline: current runtime memory planner + existing KV eviction heuristics (control) — measure peak mem, fragmentation, throughput, p99 for seq=2k/16k/32k
Prefetch-only: implement prefetch scheduler that anticipates hot KV slices at request start and places them preferentially in contiguous slabs — measure delta vs baseline
Allocator-only: expose allocator hint API and bias hybrid-slab allocator to reserve contiguous regions for prefetched KV — measure reduction in fragmentation
Combined: full kernel-aware prefetch + allocator hint + batching coordination — expected best result
A/B traffic experiment in Dedicated: start 1% traffic -> 10% -> 25% with observability on cost per token, tail latency, and OOM signals
initial_design_notes: Introduce a small model profile blob (protobuf/json) with fields: preferred_slab_size_hint, kernel_contiguity_preference, kv_prefetch_window_tokens, eviction_penalty_weight — runtime will read profiles at model load time
Prefetch scheduler will run at request enqueue, compute token window heuristics based on recent prefix usage and model profile, and make allocation reservations
Allocator hinting API will present a soft reservation (best-effort) to the GPU allocator; when reservation fails, fall back to existing paths to avoid increased latency
Batching coordinator will prefer to aggregate requests with similar profile hints to maximize contiguous allocation reuse and reduce churn
tradeoffs_and_risks: Complexity: introducing model profile semantics increases model onboarding cost; must provide tooling to auto-generate hints from offline profiling
Fragility: incorrect prefetch window or over-aggressive reservations could increase peak mem or cause wasted reserved space — conservative defaults required
Compatibility: private/on-prem customers may run older kernels/allocators; feature must gracefully degrade
Correctness: ensure prefetching doesn't change model outputs (purely memory-level) and doesn't introduce timing-dependent behavior for function-calls or stateful models
implementation_tasks: 1) Profile representative kernels for Llama/Mistral/Qwen across sequences (ENG-heatmap job) — produce initial profile blobs
2) Implement model-profile loader and schema validation at model load
3) Build prefetch scheduler in serving runtime; add metric hooks for prefetch hits/misses
4) Extend hybrid slab allocator with 'soft_reserve' hints and contiguous allocation path
5) Add batching coordinator policy to group compatible profile requests
6) Run large-scale benchmarks on dedicated fleet (2k/16k/32k) and collect metrics
7) Add runtime config flags and Console toggles for Dedicated/Hosted tiers
8) PR, design review, and incremental rollout plan
9) Update docs and onboarding scripts to generate profiles
rollout_plan: Dev: unit tests + microbenchmarks on developer GPU rigs
Canary: enable on internal staging cluster at 5% traffic for non-SLA customers, observe 48h
Beta: enable on select Dedicated customers with low-risk workloads, 10% traffic each for 2 weeks
Gradual deploy: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with monitoring checks at each step
Rollback: immediate toggle off via feature flag if OOMs increase beyond threshold or p99 latency regresses beyond acceptance criteria
monitoring_and_observability: New metrics: prefetch_bytes_reserved, prefetch_alloc_failures, contiguous_alloc_success_rate, kv_prefetch_hit_ratio
Dashboards: per-model peak mem heatmap, allocation churn graph, eviction vs prefetch correlation
Alerts: >3 OOMs/hour on canary nodes, >10% increase in eviction rate for production models
dependencies_notes: Requires integration with memory profiling infra from ENG-72654 (memory-heatmap-calibration) for initial profiling output
Align with kernel selection and quantization recommendations from ENG-915432 for combined effect analysis
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after spike analysis on long-context Llama flows — saw repeated mini-evictions during large batched generations causing tail latency spikes.
2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Design review scheduled. Proposed soft-reserve API to avoid hard allocations on missing drivers.
2026-03-12 - Engineering notes: early microbenchmarks indicate contiguous placement can reduce memcpy overheads on certain kernels by ~6% — promising for Mistral variants.
2026-03-13 - Perf testing update: prefetch-only prototype reduced fragmentation index by 12% on Qwen-32k but increased peak reserved bytes by 4% — need to tune window size.
2026-03-14 - PM sync (Jia Huang): prioritize for next release if combined experiments maintain throughput and reduce cost-per-token by >5% for enterprise workloads.
notes: This approach intentionally separates hints from enforcement: profiles guide placement but allocator retains final authority to avoid regressions on unsupported hardware.
Provide a profile generator CLI that takes an offload run and emits recommended slab/kv hints to reduce onboarding friction.
next_steps: Run full combined experiment matrix on dedicated 4xA100 nodes (seq=2k/16k/32k; batch shapes: [1,4,8] requests), collect metrics, and iterate on profile defaults
Prepare PR for model-profile schema and allocator soft_reserve API
Schedule cross-team review with Allocator owners and Console for toggles
